A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWE-SQL work. All main-text and appendix content is available for comparison, including equations, algorithms, tables, figures, prompts, and examples. V4's shorter bibliography and appendix relabeling do not represent missing scientific material.

before.justification: V3 reports original model evaluations on BIRD-CRITIC, BIRD-FIXER training results, trajectory-generation comparisons, ablations, and error analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–4, Figure 6, and the supplementary analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: SQL-Rewind, SQL-ACT, f-Plan Boosting, and Generative Thought Mode retain the same procedures. Sections 4–5 and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged apart from citation and appendix labels.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 530 PostgreSQL and 570 multi-dialect BIRD-CRITIC tasks and SIX-GYM training coverage. The preliminary workflow-integrated scenario discussed in the limitations is also retained.

E2.justification: The model comparators in Tables 2–3, SQL-ACT versus Tool-ACT comparison in Figure 4, and trajectory-generation comparators in Tables 4 and 9 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Training/evaluation database separation, task-success criteria, model configurations, inference settings, and trajectory-sampling budgets are unchanged. Appendix 16's experimental settings are retained in Appendix G.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablations in Figure 6, error analysis in Section 6.6 and Figure 8, synthetic-data validation and complexity analysis in Tables 8–9, and illustrative debugging examples.

E5.justification: Appendix 16.2 in v3 and Appendix G.2 in v4 both report averaging results over five repeated trials. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, both report O3-mini at 38.87%/33.33% on PG/MULTI and Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B BIRD-FIXER at 38.11%/29.65%, with identical trajectory-generation and ablation results.

T1.justification: The task mapping in Equation 1, trajectory and functional-plan definitions, GTM formulation, and success-rate formula are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark-novelty, SQL-debugging difficulty, trajectory-augmentation, compact-model performance, and cross-dialect generalization claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning query diversity, dialect differences, GTM, and model errors are unchanged. Appendix 18 becomes Appendix I while retaining the workflow-performance limitation and need for richer user interaction.

D1.justification: Database versions, Docker setup, annotation instructions, model aliases, library versions, hardware, LoRA settings, training times, prompts, and resource-access information are retained. Their appendix labels and citation numbers change only.

R1.justification: V4 consolidates duplicate entries for Program of Thoughts, LoRA, DIN-SQL, and Spider, reducing 57 bibliography entries to 53 while retaining every distinct work. Citation identities and the research positioning in Section 7 remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendices 10–22 become A–M, with corresponding contents and cross-reference updates. Duplicate references are consolidated and citations renumbered. Prose is otherwise unchanged except for an introduced stray 'w' after 'capabilities.' in Section 6.2.

P2.justification: Bibliography deduplication causes limited reflow and moves the appendix block one page earlier. Appendix labels and Figure 3's appendix pointer are updated; the tables, plots, diagrams, and examples retain their content and visual arrangements.

improvement.justification: Consolidating four duplicated references modestly improves bibliographic consistency, while appendix relabeling preserves all content and cross-references. This is a small editorial gain, with unchanged scientific evidence and reproducibility information; the stray 'w' introduced in Section 6.2 is a minor countervailing blemish.
